extraction.name: SWE-rebench
extraction.description: A public dataset of more than 21,000 interactive Python-based software engineering tasks collected automatically from GitHub repositories for training and benchmarking software engineering agents.
extraction.creator: Ibragim Badertdinov, Alexander Golubev, Maksim Nekrashevich, Anton Shevtsov, Simon Karasik, Andrei Andriushchenko, Maria Trofimova, Daria Litvintseva, Boris Yangel
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected through a fully automated four-stage pipeline: preliminary task collection from GitHub Archive and GitHub, automated installation instruction configuration, execution-based installation verification, and automated quality assessment.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web API, Software Collection, Document analysis
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data came from GitHub Archive daily JSON event archives and cloned GitHub repositories with full commit histories, including issue descriptions, discussions, linked pull requests, metadata, and repository files.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The authors merged data from multiple sources, linked issues with pull requests, filtered for Python repositories with permissive licenses and resolved merged PRs, required tests and limited file changes, split each PR patch into solution and test patches, grouped tasks by normalized project version, and froze dependency versions after successful setup.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Task instances were annotated automatically with LLM-generated quality labels for Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, and Test Patch Correctness by fine-tuning Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct on human annotations from SWE-bench Verified and predicting each label independently.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper reports validation performance of the fine-tuned annotation model and notes that the automated assessment is imperfect but provided as metadata for filtering and task selection.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset and benchmark are intended to be continuously updated with fresh tasks, and future work includes keeping the benchmark up to date by maintaining evaluation on fresh tasks and evaluating more models.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark may accelerate development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering, which could create risks such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse for introducing vulnerabilities; the authors argue that openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking help mitigate these concerns.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is restricted to Python repositories under permissive open-source licenses, and the automated pipeline relies on heuristics and LLM-driven interpretations that can introduce errors.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The fully automated pipeline may produce imperfectly described or unsolvable tasks, automated installation was validated on only 18 repositories for prompt engineering, automated quality assessment cannot fully replicate human judgment, and the initial release is limited to Python.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed to train and benchmark software engineering agents, particularly for reinforcement learning-based approaches, and the benchmark subset is used for standardized evaluation of LLM-based agents.

name.evidence: Using this pipeline, we construct SWE-rebench, a public dataset comprising over 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks, suitable for reinforcement leaming of SWE agents at scale.

inLanguage.evidence: The problem statement must be in English.

isLiveDataset.evidence: we introduce a novel, automated, and scalable pipeline to continuously extract real-world interactive SWE tasks from diverse GitHub repositories.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Our pipeline comprises four stages: preliminary task collection, automated installation instruction configuration, execution-based installation verification, and quality assessment, which are fully described in this section.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence:
The primary sources for our data are GitHub Archive [Grigorik, 2011] and GitHub.
We clone relevant GitHub repositories with their full commit histories to our local storage.
An LLM scans repository files (e.g., README.md, Dockerfile, setup.py) to find potential sources of installation information.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence:
The GitHub Archive is a major source of public events on GitHub. Each day, it publishes a JSON archive listing all GitHub events from that day. We use this archive to collect detailed data about issues: issue description, discussion, linked pull requests, and metadata such as creation date and labels.
We clone relevant GitHub repositories with their full commit histories to our local storage.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: To initiate the dataset building process, we download approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence:
In the first stage, we download raw input data from multiple origins, merge them, and perform preliminary filtering.
We then link issues with pull requests that mention resolving them in their title or description, applying filters to select instances where:
• The issue is from a Python repository with a permissive license.
• The issue is marked as resolved.
• The PR is merged into the main branch.
• The PR is not linked to multiple issues.
• The issue description is longer than 10 characters.
• The PR must introduces or modifies tests and includes code changes beyond test files.
• Changes affect 1 to 15 files.
For each selected pull request, the overall patch is divided into two components: a solution patch, containing changes to non-test files intended to address the issue, and a test patch, comprising only changes to test files.
We group these task instances by project versions inferred from git tag outputs, normalizing versions to major.minor format (e.g., 1.2.3 is normalized to 1.2).
Record exact dependency versions (via pip freeze, conda env export) after a successful setup to mitigate reproducibility issues from unpinned dependencies in Python projects, ensuring consistent environment recreation in the future.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence:
To assess these properties automatically, we fine-tune an instruction-following model using human annotations from SWE-bench Verified to predict:
• Issue Clarity
• Task Complexity
• Test Patch Correctness
We fine-tune Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct using annotations from SWE-bench Verified.
It is then prompted to predict one of three binary quality labels: Issue Clarity, Task Complexity, or Test Patch Correctness.
We train the model to predict each label independently; each task instance is assessed for each quality characteristic separately using a 75/25 training/validation split (total 413 validation examples).

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence:
For Task Complexity (where 'high-score' implies >1 hour to solve; 100 high-score vs. 313 low-score examples in validation), our fine-tuned model achieved 81% accuracy and a weighted F1-score of 0.82.
For Test Patch Correctness (180 high-score vs. 233 low-score examples), the model achieved 67% accuracy (weighted F1: 0.65). For Issue Clarity (84 high-score vs. 329 low-score examples), it achieved 79% accuracy (weighted F1: 0.76).
While this automated assessment is not perfect, these labels offer users a means to filter the dataset and select task instances according to their specific criteria.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: We fine-tune Qwen 2.5-72B-Instruct using annotations from SWE-bench Verified.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence:
we introduce a novel, automated, and scalable pipeline to continuously extract real-world interactive SWE tasks from diverse GitHub repositories.
A public SWE-rebench leaderboard that offers continuously updated, decontaminated, and standardized evaluations for LLM-based agents
Keeping SWE-rebench benchmark up-to-date: Maintaining evaluation process on fresh tasks for the existing models, evaluating a wider range of LLMs and sharing detailed performance analyses with the community.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Finally, while our benchmark is intended to support transparency and standardization in evaluating SWE agents, it may also accelerate the development of increasingly autonomous AI systems in software engineering. This progress brings potential risks, such as overreliance on AI-generated code or misuse of automated agents for introducing vulnerabilities. We believe that fostering openness, decontaminated evaluations, and rigorous benchmarking practices helps mitigate these concems and contributes to responsible advancement of the field.

rai:dataBiases.evidence:
To initiate the dataset building process, we download approximately 450,000 pull requests linked to issues created before May 1, 2025. These originate from over 30,000 repositories that feature permissive licenses granting broad usage rights ... and where Python constitutes over 75% of the codebase lines of code.
While our multi-stage filtering, refinements to existing methodologies and automated dependency installation are designed for robustness at scale, they rely on heuristics and LLM-driven interpretations.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence:
However, the emphasis on scalability introduces trade-offs, particularly a reduced ability to manually curate and verify the quality and clarity of each individual task.
For instance, our LLM-based approach to generating installation instructions from repository files (Qwen2.5-72B-Instruct, Section 2.2), while far more scalable than manual methods, was validated on a limited set of 18 repositories for prompt engineering and may not capture every project's subtleties.
Similarly, the automated task quality assessment (Section 2.4), where an LLM is fine-tuned on SWE-bench Verified task labels to predict complexity and relevance, serves as a valuable scalable proxy but cannot fully replicate nuanced human judgment, thus, containing errors and decreasing quality of the datasets.
Limited language diversity: The initial release of SWE-rebench is limited exclusively to Python, restricting its immediate applicability to other language ecosystems.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence:
SWE-rebench2, a public dataset of more than 21,000 interactive Python-based SWE tasks, designed to train and benchmark agents in diverse executable environments, particularly suitable for reinforcement leaming-based approaches.
It serves as the foundation for SWE-rebench public datasets and a continuously updated benchmark designed for robust and transparent evaluation of agent performance in realistic SWE scenarios.
